subject: maths
title: Highest common factor and lowest common multiple

scenes.heading: HCF and LCM
scenes.sub: When will two buses leave together again?
scenes.say: Two buses leave at the same time but run on different timetables. When will they leave together again? To answer that, you need the lowest common multiple. You'll also meet its partner, the highest common factor.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Laps every 6 and 8 minutes: both at the start line at 24 minutes
scenes.science: 24 is the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8
scenes.breaks: Real runners speed up and slow down; numbers repeat perfectly forever.
scenes.say: Two friends run laps. Ali takes six minutes a lap and Ben takes eight. Ali crosses the start line at six, twelve, eighteen, twenty-four. Ben crosses at eight, sixteen, twenty-four. They first cross together at twenty-four minutes. That's the lowest common multiple of six and eight.

scenes.heading: The two ideas
points: HCF: biggest number that divides into both
LCM: smallest number both divide into
scenes.say: The highest common factor, or H C F, is the biggest number that divides into both numbers. The H C F of eighteen and twenty-four is six. The lowest common multiple, or L C M, is the smallest number that both divide into. The L C M of six and eight is twenty-four.

scenes.heading: Common factors of 18 and 24
notes: Common factors go in the overlap
The biggest one in the overlap is the HCF
scenes.say: Here's a Venn diagram. First the factors of eighteen, then the factors of twenty-four. The common factors, one, two, three and six, sit in the overlap. The biggest one there, six, is the H C F.
scenes.caption: Common factors 1, 2, 3, 6 → HCF = 6

scenes.heading: Multiples of 6 and 8 meet at 24
notes: Jump in sixes above, eights below
scenes.say: Now jump along a number line in sixes above and in eights below. The first number they both land on is twenty-four, so the L C M of six and eight is twenty-four.
scenes.caption: LCM of 6 and 8 = 24

scenes.heading: Worked example: HCF
scenes.question: Find the HCF of 12 and 18.
scenes.say: Find the H C F of twelve and eighteen. List the factors of each. The numbers in both lists are one, two, three and six. The biggest is six, so the H C F is six.

scenes.heading: Worked example: LCM
scenes.question: Find the LCM of 4 and 10.
scenes.say: Now find the L C M of four and ten. List multiples of the bigger number, ten. Ten doesn't divide by four, but twenty does. So the L C M is twenty.

scenes.heading: Which one do I need?
scenes.say: Which one do you need? Splitting things into equal groups, or the biggest group size, means H C F. Happening together again, or the smallest amount to match, means L C M. The H C F is small, and the L C M is big.

Quick recap. The H C F is the biggest factor of both numbers. The L C M is the smallest multiple of both. Sharing means H C F, together again means L C M. And multiplying the numbers doesn't always give the L C M. Now try the practice questions!
